title: Maple Ridge Home Energy Rebates 2026: Heat Pumps, Insulation and Windows
desc: Maple Ridge rebates for 2026 from BC Hydro, FortisBC and CleanBC, with 2021 Census numbers on a city where 79% of households own.
badge: Up to $5,500 for insulation, $4,000 for a heat pump
lead: Maple Ridge has 33,110 households, 79% of them owners and 53% in detached houses. Few BC cities combine that much ownership with that many houses, which is exactly who the home rebates are written for.
cards_heading: What you can claim in Maple Ridge in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts come from the program pages we re-read on October 2, 2026. Each card is a maximum, and most depend on how your home is heated.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: Must replace electric heat such as baseboards or an electric furnace, meet 100% of the heating load at -5C and be installed by a Home Performance Contractor Network member.

cards.title: Partial heat pump
cards.note: For a heat pump that covers at least half of the heating load while replacing electric heat.

cards.title: Limited-time bonus
cards.note: Extra money on heat pump installs completed between August 1 and October 31, 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified switch from gas, oil or propane
cards.note: CleanBC pays by income level (Level 3 / Level 2 / Level 1) for a central or three-head heat pump, for invoices from July 6, 2026.

cards.title: Insulation
cards.note: Attic, wall and basement or crawlspace work, paid per R-value added per square foot. Homes heated mainly by electricity only.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: $100 per opening, with a U-factor of 1.22 or lower.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Only when it replaces an electric water heater.

cards.title: Solar panels
cards.note: $1,000 per kW, capped at half the cost, from an HPCN member installer.

cards.title: Battery storage
cards.note: Up to $1,500 on its own with solar, or up to $5,000 with Peak Saver enrolment.

cards.title: EV charger
cards.note: 50% of a new wall-mounted Level 2 charger, plus $200 for a power-management device.

sections: In the 2021 Census, 29% of Maple Ridge households lived in homes built before 1981, and 5,160 of those homes are owner-occupied detached houses. Major repairs were reported by 4.8%. Maple Ridge has the second-highest owner share in the group after the Township of Langley. For an electric-heated house the BC Hydro rebates up to $4,000 (heat pump), $5,500 (insulation), $2,000 (windows) and $1,000 (water heater) can all apply to the same project.

Where homes sit away from gas lines, propane or oil is common, and BC Hydro will not rebate a heat pump that replaces those fuels. CleanBC pays $3,500, $7,000 or $13,000 for income-qualified households who switch to a central or three-head heat pump. We cannot say how many Maple Ridge homes use each fuel, so check your own bills.
Colder than the rest of the Lower Mainland

The 2015 to 2024 record low was -19.6°C, which is lower than Burnaby, Richmond or Surrey, although the January average low is a mild 0.1°C. Size the heat pump to BC Hydro's -5°C rule and ask the installer what the unit does at -15°C.
Solar here gets about 3.19 peak sun hours a day, the lowest figure in our data. Rebates up to $5,000 for solar and up to $5,000 for a battery with Peak Saver are available but depend on funding.

claim_heading: Where to start in Maple Ridge
claim_steps: Measure insulation depth in the attic and ask for R-value quotes.
Get two HPCN quotes for the heat pump.
Ask about CleanBC if income is lower.
faq: Yes, 79% of households own according to the 2021 Census.
What is the coldest it gets?
The record low in 2015 to 2024 was -19.6 degrees Celsius.
Do I get both insulation and window rebates?
Yes, they are separate programs with separate caps, and a bonus of up to $2,000 applies to multiple upgrades.
From BC Hydro, yes. CleanBC may still apply on income.
